# v0.1.0 visual polish: colours, sprite scaling, Gen V stills (2026-11-23)

## Colour bug
- **Cause:** `h()` in `ui/js/core.js` applied object styles with `Object.assign(el.style, …)`. For CSS custom properties such as `{'--tc': …}` this only creates a plain JavaScript property, so the variable never reached CSS.
- **Effects:**
  - Type badges fell back to `var(--tc, #555)`, which is grey.
  - Stat bars fell back to `var(--accent)` (#eef1f4), which is near-white.
  - Showcase `--sc-alpha`/`--sc-cols` and silhouette colours were affected the same way.
- **Fix:** a `setStyle()` helper uses `style.setProperty()` for `--*` keys. A test checks the actual `getComputedStyle()` result.
- **Type badges:** colours now come from `.t-<type>` classes using the existing `tokens.css` palette, covering 17 types (no Fairy).
  - Labels use dark ink on 12 lighter types (Normal, Fire, Water, Electric, Grass, Ice, Ground, Flying, Psychic, Bug, Rock, Steel) and white on Fighting, Poison, Ghost, Dragon and Dark.
  - Every badge reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast.
- **Stat bars:**
  - The Better Default soft colour is set on each row, giving a tinted label edge and a lightly shaded bar.
  - The Total row is neutral.
  - Bars are drawn against 255 (and 720 for the total), so proportions are exact instead of clipping at 180.
  - Appearance › Stat bars › Accent now uses one restrained colour (`--stat-single`) instead of the near-white app accent, which looked like the bug.

## Sprite scaling
- PokéAPI's Gen V animations are already cropped to the Pokémon: the frame bounds equal the canvas, measured over all frames. Their natural sizes are therefore the true relative sizes, e.g. Charmander 41, Charmeleon 66, Charizard 89 and Lugia 153 px.
- **Old rule:** the largest whole-number scale that filled a 96/200 px box. Charmander became 4× (168 px) and Charizard 2× (178 px), almost the same size.
- **New rule (`artImage()` / `artScale()`):**
  - One fixed scale per view: frames of at least 180 px use 2×, smaller frames 1×.
  - Art is shrunk only when it would not fit; it is never enlarged to fill, never stretched, and keeps its aspect ratio.
  - Shrinking uses smoothing.
  - A ResizeObserver refits the art when the window is resized.
- **Frames:**
  - In-app Summary: 240×212 (2×); under 720 px wide: 120×112 (1×).
  - Popouts: compact 112×104 (1×), standard 136×120 (1×), expanded 220×196 (2×).
- **Result:** Charmander 82 → Charmeleon 132 → Charizard 174/178 px in the Summary. Stills (96 px canvas) use the same scale.

## Grid and Home/Live
- **Grid:** uses the library's Gen V stills (one style with the Summaries).
  - Each still is trimmed to its visible bounds, which the sprite library measures with a stdlib PNG reader at import. A one-time background backfill covers libraries installed earlier.
  - Small Pokémon are enlarged at most 1.5× and large ones are shrunk to fit; tile sizes are unchanged.
  - The grid has no animations. Without a library, the client box icons are used as before.
- **Home rows, roamers and favourites:** Gen V stills.
- **Live detail:** one animated sprite, unless reduced motion or the pause setting is on.
- Reports that name no species, or several, keep the neutral icon. The parser and provider are unchanged.

## Not verified
- The native Qt (XCB/Wayland) shell was not run here; only the Qt stub test and headless Chrome were.
- Animated sprites were measured from the real PokéAPI files; the UI tests use generated GIFs with the same sizes.
